golden_baseline_location: Regenerated, never copied: `make legacy-etl-gen-data NS=<ns>` then `make legacy-etl-run JOB=sftp_ingest_poll` under `OTTERWORKS_LEGACY_ROOT=/home/ubuntu/otterworks-legacy-<ns>` via scripts/tp-run-deterministic.sh. Baseline = the seeded `sftp-drop/upload/CUSTBILL*.dat` bytes (2 files, 52 lines each incl. HDR/TRL) and the legacy `incoming/` copies.

behaviour.input: Every `CUSTBILL*.dat` under `/Volumes/ow_tp/bronze/landing/<ns>/incoming/` (the producer or the parent's `custbill.py land` writes there; see D7-1).
steps: For each file: read bytes once, compute sha256, write `archive/<basename>.<sha256[:12]>` (content-addressed, not wall-clock), re-read archive and compare hashes; only then delete the incoming copy.
Load every line into ow_tp.bronze.custbill_raw with ns, source_file, line_no (1-based), record_kind (HDR if line starts 'HDR', TRL if 'TRL', else BODY), raw_line unchanged, file_sha256, ingested_at.
Idempotency: a file whose sha256 already exists in bronze for this ns is skipped (logged as duplicate), not re-inserted; a rerun with no new files inserts 0 rows.
Loading is `DELETE ... WHERE ns=? AND source_file=? AND file_sha256=?` then INSERT for that file only; never DDL, never touch other ns.
behaviour.settle_protocol: No size-twice heuristic. A file is eligible only if its name has no `.part`/`.tmp` suffix; producers are asked to write-then-rename (D3-3/R1). Half-written files are therefore a declared coverage gap on the producer side, not a heuristic in the job.

encoding_policy.input_encoding: ASCII (fixture FACT); production EBCDIC/other is a coverage gap pending R1
encoding_policy.byte_transparency: raw_line must be byte-identical to the source line minus the trailing `\n`; no trimming, no re-encoding; archive copy byte-identical to source (sha256 equal)
encoding_policy.invalid_bytes: non-UTF-8 bytes: file is loaded (raw_line via latin-1 decode) and flagged in the run log; never dropped silently

malformed_record_policy.details: Ingest is byte-transparent: every line, whatever its length or content, becomes exactly one bronze row attributed to (ns, source_file, line_no). Nothing is validated here; validation is the parse unit's job.

empty_input_semantics.details: No `CUSTBILL*.dat` present → task succeeds, inserts 0 rows, logs 'no files'. A zero-byte file → archived, 0 bronze rows, logged as empty (not an error).

planted_anomalies.reason: The volume producer (parent `custbill.py land`, later the customer landing mechanism per R4) writes whole files; there is no partial-write fixture. Contract requires write-then-rename from the producer.

planted_anomalies.description: Landing the same file twice yields one bronze copy (sha256 dedupe) and a 'duplicate' log line.

acceptance_checks.description: Per file: incoming byte count == archive byte count == legacy source byte count; sha256(archive) == sha256(source).
count(*) FROM ow_tp.bronze.custbill_raw WHERE ns=? AND source_file=? == `wc -l` of the legacy file (52) for each of the 2 files; record_kind counts HDR=1, TRL=1, BODY=50 per file.
Byte parity: concat(raw_line ORDER BY line_no) + '\n' per line == legacy file bytes.
Idempotency: second run with no new files inserts 0 rows; re-landing the same file inserts 0 rows and logs duplicate; counts identical.
Incoming copy is deleted only after archive hash verification (inspect run log ordering + volume listing after run).

deficiencies_retired: hostname if-blocks / hardcoded paths → `ns` parameter + volume paths
lock file never removed → max_concurrent_runs=1 on the job, lock-free idempotent load
size-twice settle heuristic → hash-verified archive + producer rename protocol
cp ... || true; rm → verify-then-delete, errors raised
archive/ grows forever with wall-clock names → content-addressed archive; retention is a D-entry (not this unit)

run_mode_budget.child: own ns slice `<unit>-w1` in ow_tp tables + volume; report run_mode=live with that namespace; never NS=demo
run_mode_budget.parent: single uncontended window on NS=demo per wave
